# date-fns Internationalization Examples

> Locale resolution, localized names and week-start conventions. See [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) for the
> decisions and [reference.md](../reference.md) for the locale-aware format tokens.

---

## Resolving a Locale

date-fns locales are values you pass, not global state. One module owns the map so a missing
regional variant falls back to its language rather than to English.

```typescript
// date-locales.ts
import { enUS, enGB, de, fr, es, ja, zhCN, ptBR, ar } from "date-fns/locale";
import type { Locale } from "date-fns";

const DEFAULT_LOCALE = enUS;

const locales: Record<string, Locale> = {
  "en-US": enUS,
  "en-GB": enGB,
  "en-AU": enGB, // closer than enUS on dates
  "de-DE": de,
  "fr-FR": fr,
  "es-ES": es,
  "ja-JP": ja,
  "zh-CN": zhCN,
  "pt-BR": ptBR,
  "ar-SA": ar,
};

export function getDateLocale(localeCode: string): Locale {
  if (locales[localeCode]) return locales[localeCode];

  // "de-CH" → any "de-*" entry before giving up
  const language = localeCode.split("-")[0];
  const match = Object.entries(locales).find(([key]) =>
    key.startsWith(`${language}-`),
  );

  return match ? match[1] : DEFAULT_LOCALE;
}
```

Every locale you name is bundled, so the map is also the list of what ships — a dynamic
`import(\`date-fns/locale/${code}\`)` trades bundle size for a round trip.

---

## Formatting with a Locale

The `P`-family tokens carry the locale's own ordering and separators, which is the whole point of
passing a locale rather than branching on one.

```typescript
import { format, formatDistanceToNow } from "date-fns";
import { getDateLocale } from "./date-locales";

function formatDate(date: Date, localeCode: string, pattern = "PP"): string {
  return format(date, pattern, { locale: getDateLocale(localeCode) });
}

formatDate(date, "en-US", "P"); // "01/15/2026"
formatDate(date, "de-DE", "P"); // "15.01.2026"
formatDate(date, "ja-JP", "P"); // "2026/01/15"

formatDate(date, "de-DE", "PPPP"); // "Donnerstag, 15. Januar 2026"
formatDate(date, "ar-SA", "PPPP"); // "الخميس، 15 يناير 2026"

// The same option reaches the relative functions
formatDistanceToNow(date, {
  locale: getDateLocale("fr-FR"),
  addSuffix: true,
}); // "il y a 14 jours"
```

## Localized Month and Weekday Names

Generate them by formatting reference dates, so the locale supplies the strings rather than a table
you maintain.

```typescript
import { format, startOfWeek, addDays } from "date-fns";
import { getDateLocale } from "./date-locales";

// "LLLL" is the standalone month form — several languages inflect it
// differently from the "MMMM" used inside a full date
function getMonthNames(localeCode: string, pattern: "LLLL" | "LLL" = "LLLL") {
  const locale = getDateLocale(localeCode);
  return Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, month) =>
    format(new Date(2026, month, 1), pattern, { locale }),
  );
}

function getWeekdayNames(
  localeCode: string,
  pattern: "EEEE" | "EEE" | "EEEEE" = "EEEE",
  weekStartsOn: 0 | 1 = 0,
) {
  const locale = getDateLocale(localeCode);
  const anySunday = new Date(2026, 0, 4);
  const start = startOfWeek(anySunday, { weekStartsOn });

  return Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) =>
    format(addDays(start, i), pattern, { locale }),
  );
}

getMonthNames("ja-JP"); // ["1月", "2月", …]

// "EEE" is the abbreviated width, which German writes with a trailing point;
// "EEEEEE" is the short width, which does not
getWeekdayNames("de-DE", "EEE", 1); // ["Mo.", "Di.", "Mi.", "Do.", "Fr.", "Sa.", "So."]
```

## Week Start Day

`weekStartsOn` defaults to Sunday and is not inferred from the locale you pass, so a calendar has to
supply it. Three conventions are in wide use, including Saturday.

```typescript
import { startOfWeek, endOfWeek, eachDayOfInterval, format } from "date-fns";
import { getDateLocale } from "./date-locales";

const DEFAULT_WEEK_START = 1; // Monday — ISO 8601

const WEEK_START_BY_LOCALE: Record<string, 0 | 1 | 6> = {
  "en-US": 0,
  "en-CA": 0,
  "ja-JP": 0,
  "zh-CN": 0, // Sunday
  "en-GB": 1,
  "de-DE": 1,
  "fr-FR": 1,
  "ru-RU": 1, // Monday
  "ar-SA": 6,
  "ar-AE": 6, // Saturday
};

const weekStartFor = (localeCode: string) =>
  WEEK_START_BY_LOCALE[localeCode] ?? DEFAULT_WEEK_START;

function getCalendarWeek(date: Date, localeCode: string) {
  const locale = getDateLocale(localeCode);
  const weekStartsOn = weekStartFor(localeCode);

  return eachDayOfInterval({
    start: startOfWeek(date, { weekStartsOn }),
    end: endOfWeek(date, { weekStartsOn }),
  }).map((day) => ({ date: day, label: format(day, "EEE", { locale }) }));
}

// For 2026-01-15: en-US runs Jan 11–17, de-DE runs Jan 12–18, ar-SA runs Jan 10–16
```

## Where the Platform Is Enough

`Intl.DateTimeFormat` needs no locale import and no bundle bytes, and it reads the full CLDR data
the runtime already carries. Reach for date-fns when the operation is arithmetic, comparison or
relative phrasing.

```typescript
import { formatDistanceToNow } from "date-fns";
import { getDateLocale } from "./date-locales";

// Display only — no bundled locale
const display = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(localeCode, {
  dateStyle: "medium",
  timeStyle: "short",
}).format(date);

const monthNames = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, month) =>
  new Intl.DateTimeFormat(localeCode, { month: "long" }).format(
    new Date(2026, month, 1),
  ),
);

// Relative phrasing across arbitrary distances — this is date-fns's job
const ago = formatDistanceToNow(date, {
  locale: getDateLocale(localeCode),
  addSuffix: true,
});
```
